title: One executable description of CI, and a plugin that ships only what it runs
description: F1 of CONSOLIDATED-PLAN.md (quality-gates-internal, reports/2026-10-14-cost-code-ci-analysis, section 2.2; owner approval 2026-10-14 in DECISIONS.md, V1-V9). It touches the plugin's behaviour toward a user in two places only: `--selftest` on shipped entry points and `render-report --bench` go away (neither is promised by COMPATIBILITY.md), plus the falsifier, which the owner retired (2026-10-16, P128.17's cancellation). The CI half touches tools/ and .github/ only. Invariants established: I11 (plugins/audit/ holds only what the installed copy runs), I12 (B9 recorded at F1.5's landing SHA), I13 (a screenshot is stale exactly when what the page receives changed), I14-I17 (one executable gate description, a matrix derived from conditions, intermittents sought on purpose on the release tier, a verified SHA not re-run). ORDER: every task that edits plugins/audit/tests/ lands before F1.4 moves that directory to tests/, so F1.6, F1.6-falsifier and F1.7 run at their 571becfd paths and before the move, not after it as the plan had them; F1.5 follows F1.4. Stop criteria (plan section 5): F1.2 stops if a stress-only or stress-misses difference repeats in two attempts or the median wall exceeds 8m59s over at least five runs; F1.4-F1.5 stop if the prove-gates name set changes unexplained, a lint checks fewer references without a named reason, tests/ reaches the installed cache, the product imports from tools/, or the whole repo changes by 0.5k lines or more for a move; F1 ends only with B9 recorded and the repo smaller, not merely rearranged. Every figure was re-measured at 571becfd; the companion F1-NOTES.md carries each one, old beside new, with its command.
desiredOutcome: Every CI job is setup plus one `tools/verify.sh --only <slices>` call and a SHA already green on every job is not run again on main; every sweep leg is graded by the plain rules; the installed plugin carries no tests/, no lint modules, no demo generator and no bench, and its bytes are at most 10,416,128; B9 is recorded with the SHA it was measured at; a prose edit in _ui_theme.py no longer owes a screenshot recapture; and the retired lints and the falsifier are gone with their cases and prove-gates rows.

findings.issue: The comment still says `ui_surface_digests()` hashes `_ui_theme.py` 'as a member of BOTH surfaces, reading raw bytes', and that a CRLF checkout therefore moved every digest. The diff deletes `ui_surface_digests()` and `_UI_TOKEN_LAYER`. The digest is now taken over the imported page text, so the file is no longer read as raw bytes (Python normalises source newlines on import). The comment names a function that no longer exists and gives a reason that no longer holds. The executor could not edit it because the plan gate refused the file.
findings.resolution: Rewrite the comment to say what the `_ui_theme.py text eol=lf` pin is still for, or drop the pin and the comment together if nothing else reads the file's bytes. Do it in a task that declares .gitattributes.

findings.issue: The comment says the anchor's walk needs the same directory for `ui_surface_digests()`, 'in the anchor, for the screenshot rule'. That function is removed by this diff. The anchor now holds `ui_surface_sources()`, and the digest lives in `_surface_digest.py`. The executor could not edit it because the plan gate refused the file.
findings.resolution: Change it to `ui_surface_sources()` and drop 'for the screenshot rule'. The plan gate currently lists P130.7, P130.8 and P130.9 as declaring this file, so make the edit under one of them.

findings.issue: The retired $defs/falsifier keeps its property descriptions in the present tense. `find` still says the drive 'reports [a missing find] as could-not-run', `command` says it is 'run from the copy's root', and `timeout` says 'Absent reads `drive-phase.py`'s FALSIFIER_TIMEOUT'. That constant is deleted by this diff (fp0b asserts it is gone), so the sentence names a symbol that no longer exists and describes behaviour nothing performs. The task asked for the field to be 'described as retired and read by nothing'. Only the parent and the def itself were reworded.
findings.resolution: Reword the five property descriptions in the past tense or reduce them to 'retired, read by nothing'. Delete the FALSIFIER_TIMEOUT reference.

findings.issue: The diff regenerates this module-map line (drive-phase no longer imports _manifest_rules). PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md is in the stamp's dirtyPaths but not in the stamp's `scope`, and is not in the brief's diff command. It is an undeclared change to the task, so a `done --commit` could refuse over it as a path no in_progress task covers, and it escapes this diff's review.
findings.resolution: Run `audit-task.py scope P130.6 --files ...,PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md` before the close, or commit that file under the task.

findings.issue: The comment says a run on main 'is the record of what landed and is never cancelled'. `cancel-in-progress: false` only stops a RUNNING run being cancelled. GitHub still cancels a PENDING run when a newer run queues in the same group `ci-refs/heads/main`. Two pushes to main in quick succession, or a push while a dispatch on main is queued, can leave a main SHA with a cancelled run. CHANGELOG.md says 'everywhere but main' with the same implication. Read from GitHub's concurrency semantics; not exercised.
findings.resolution: Reword the comment to say a RUNNING main run is never cancelled and a queued one can be replaced, or key the group on the SHA on main so main runs never share a group.

findings.issue: 'Every per-run slice has a job' reads a job's `if:` only for `inputs.tier == 'release'`. Mutated copies with `if: ${{ false }}` on browser-panel, and a push-only condition on browser-panel, both returned [] for slice_drift and shard_matrix_drift (lines 1609-1642). The claim holds only for the one condition shape it reads.
findings.resolution: Treat a job `if:` as the known per-run guard only when it reduces to the verified-run guard, optionally with the release-tier term; otherwise report it as a condition the reader cannot prove runs on every run. Add sv cases for `if: false` and a push-only condition.

findings.issue: `decide()` matches on `head_sha` and `path` but never on the run's `event` (ask_github at 162-165). A pull_request run's `head_sha` is the PR head while its checkout is the merge commit; if main later receives that SHA by fast-forward, the PR run vouches for a tree it never tested and every main job is skipped. The docstring's 'exactly this commit' holds for workflow_dispatch and push only.
findings.resolution: Fetch `event` with the run listing and accept only workflow_dispatch and push runs. Add a cv case where a green pull_request run on the same SHA refuses.

findings.issue: Untouched files still say ci.yml carries the launcher steps and the scale-demo step (tools/check-git-pipeline.py:11,29,38,226; plugins/audit/tests/test_gen_demo_manifest.py:729,800). This diff moved those steps into verify.sh's e2e and manifests slices.
findings.resolution: Change 'ci.yml' to tools/verify.sh's e2e slice / the manifests slice at those lines.

findings.issue: The diff rewrites the label of an unrelated existing case from `ctw29 SECOND-DIRECTION CASE` to `ctw29SECOND-DIRECTION CASE` (space deleted), a stray edit outside the task's scope that changes the case id other tooling and logs key on.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause: Acceptance says "`python3 tools/prove-gates.py` once, both directions, green for the rest; the full sweep is green". The outcome states the full prove-gates run 'was NOT completed' (about 11 lint groups proved in a scratch copy, tests_import_violations still running at submit), and the sweep 'exited 1 with 338 of 340 files ok' (test_drive_phase sc4, gate-parity vsh6/vsh9, passed alone once). Reconcile the filed selftests gate word with the recorded run.

findings.issue: Comments and documents still name mechanisms this diff deleted: `_help.schema_subset_drift()` and `_help.schema_inline_drift()` as 'the comparison' (_manifest_vocab.py), `_refs.absolute_reach_violations()` reading a docstring (guard-secrets-read.py), `_deps.SHARED_CONCERNS` (_priority.py), and in CLAUDE.md `ui_navigability_violations()` and the 'checked paragraph' claim for `isolation_drift()`. SUBSET_ANCHORS is now read by nothing, although the outcome says everything only the retired lints read went in the orphan cascade. These files are outside the changed lines but the retirement is what made the sentences false (shape crosses the boundary: the lint on one side, the sentence on the other). The executor disclosed the three code files as gate-refused and drafted the CLAUDE.md text in its outcome.

findings.issue: Files outside the brief's list were edited (cases mv23-mv27, mv29-mv32 retired, mv28/mv33 reworded, mv36 given its own source scan), and the bulk function and case deletions were made by scratchpad scripts the plan gate did not see. The outcome discloses both. The mv36 rewrite and the mv28/mv33 rewording change what a kept test asserts and are not covered by the task's tests.add.

findings.issue: The test pins the wait function (pollIntervalOf/pollWindowMs) and greps capture-screenshots.mjs for the 6500 / 6.5s literals, but nothing proves each of the eight converted sites routes through waitForPoll/sleepPollWindow. A future hand-written wait with a different number (say 7000) or a waitForFunction with an inline timeout passes both the function cases and the literal grep, so the interval and a wait can still diverge at a call site.
findings.resolution: Extend the source check to count `waitForFunction(` calls carrying a numeric `timeout:` in the poll-window sites, or assert that every `waitForTimeout(` argument in the assertLiveData/assertComboOverlay/assertGateCard bodies is the computed window. Alternatively, file it as a known limit in the test header's WHAT THIS CANNOT SEE block.

findings.issue: gate_entry_shape_problem reads a whole entry as one command, never splitting on && || ; |. Probed read-only: 'python3 a/test_x.py && python3 a/test_y.py' (two suites run in sequence, a correct entry, and the same joiner the plan's own lint gate uses) is reported as 'runs a/test_x.py as a program and hands it a/test_y.py as arguments' - a false statement - and would be refused by add, add --from-file, scope --gate and --gate-set and warned on by validate. No test covers a chained entry (gx1 quiet list has none).
findings.resolution: Cut the shell words at control operators before reading, judge each segment on its own (first path, the word before it, the extra suite paths), and add a chained-suites allow case to gx1.

findings.issue: The 'names a path twice' rule applies to every path-shaped word, not to suites. Probed: 'pytest a/test_x.py::t1 a/test_x.py::t2' (two distinct node ids) and 'python3 tools/r.py --in docs/p.json --out docs/p.json' are both refused/warned as naming a path more than once. The task says an entry naming one suite twice; an in-place tool invocation or two node ids of one file are legitimate and would be refused with no way round.
findings.resolution: Restrict the repeat rule to is_suite_path words and compare them with any '::' node id kept (or only flag when the whole word is identical); add an allow case for node ids and for a non-suite repeated path.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause: acceptance (3) and tests.add say validate-manifest reports such an entry 'already in a plan' / 'a plan already holding a malformed gate entry' as a warning; the walk warns only for a task whose status is not TERMINAL, and gx2 pins silence for a done task. A plan holding the shape in finished tasks (the very tasks the fault was filed on) validates silent. The narrowing is the executor's own reading and the comment justifies it, but the clause does not carry it.
findings.resolution: Warn for every task regardless of status (it is only a warning), or get the clause amended before narrowing; drop the done-task half of gx2 accordingly.

findings.issue: 'Run as a program' is read from the word IMMEDIATELY before the first path, so an interpreter option hides it: 'python3 -u a/test_x.py a/test_y.py' and 'python3 -X dev a/test_x.py a/test_y.py' return None (probed) although they have exactly the F720 shape. The predicate's own docstring claims the interpreter-or-nothing reading.
findings.resolution: Walk back from the first path to the segment start, skipping option words (and their values), and treat '-m <module>' as a runner; add the option case to gx1.

findings.issue: _covers_clause says a directory entry 'opens nothing until that task is started' for EVERY non-direct, non-in_progress row, including done/cancelled tasks. Before this diff a done task covering the file through a directory reached the terminal branch of _declaration_note (:~569) whose whole point is that '/audit:task start' refuses terminal work and a NEW task is the route; now _split_declared (:106-115) files it as a 'cover', the terminal branch is skipped, and the text implies starting it is the way forward. Verdicts are unchanged; the wording is false for terminal statuses, and the s7b/bt8 cases only exercise 'pending'.
findings.resolution: In _covers_clause branch on status in _TERMINAL_DECLARING_STATUSES and say 'which is terminal and is not re-started' instead of 'opens nothing until that task is started'; add a case with a done task whose directory entry covers the file.

findings.issue: The new multi-key walk and the promotion branch (`elif direct and not seen[tid]["direct"]: seen[tid].update(entry=key, direct=True)`) - a task listing both `lib/` and `lib/exact.ts` - is reached by no case: bt8 and s7b use different tasks for the directory and the exact file, and s8 reads only taskId. The entry/direct fields themselves are asserted nowhere on declaring_tasks directly (test__config.py is in the diff scope but untouched). Deleting the elif would leave every case green and would make a task that names the file itself render as a 'cover', i.e. dropped from 'declared by'.
findings.resolution: Add a declaring_tasks case (test_require_plan.py near s8 or test__config.py) with one task listing both `lib/` and `lib/exact.ts` asserting a single row with direct True and entry `lib/exact.ts`, and a row for a directory-only task asserting direct False and the entry.

findings.issue: _declaration_note's docstring still says it is keyed on 'WHICH of three causes actually holds'; the undeclared-branch now also carries a fourth state (covered only by an unstarted directory entry), which the docstring never mentions.
findings.resolution: Add one paragraph to the docstring naming the directory-cover case and that it takes the undeclared remedies.

findings.issue: The reworded comment joined two sentences onto one 148-character line ('that call rather than here; the `meta.ado` ones are described below. This module exists for the vocabularies MULTIPLE modules share, which is this'), breaking the comment's wrapped shape; every neighbouring line is wrapped near 90 columns.
findings.resolution: Re-wrap the sentence across lines at the comment's width; no wording change.

findings.issue: '`gate-parity.py` is why that cannot come back.' now follows directly after the rewritten isolation paragraph (CLAUDE.md:279-283), which says that paragraph is NOT checked and is owed by whoever adds a family. 'that' now reads as the unchecked isolation-doc drift, which the next sentence does not guard; the sentence it protects (gate-set descriptions drifting) is two lines down.
findings.resolution: Make the antecedent explicit, e.g. '`gate-parity.py` is why the drift between the gate-set descriptions cannot come back.'

findings.issue: pollDependent() flags a wait only when its call text names RUNSTATUS/pollRunStatus or carries a literal of 4+ digits >= the poll interval. A hand-written wait whose duration is a computed or named value (panelPollWindowMs(), POLL_MARGIN_MS + n, a const like PANEL_BOOT_MS/TAB_WIRED_MS at capture-screenshots.mjs:670,678) is invisible to the scan, so a hand-rolled copy of the helper's window outside waitForPoll/sleepPollWindow passes. The test's own WHAT THIS CANNOT SEE names only the sub-interval literal case.
findings.resolution: Add panelPollWindowMs|pollWindowText|POLL_MARGIN_MS|pollIntervalOf to the names pollDependent() treats as poll-dependent (they are the helpers' own window), and add one scratch-copy mutation using panelPollWindowMs() in a bare page.waitForTimeout; or extend the cannot-see note to say computed durations are unpoliced.

findings.issue: blank() is a hand-rolled tokenizer with no regex-literal and no nested-template (`${ '...' }`) handling. An unbalanced quote inside a future regex literal would desync it and blank the rest of the file, silently dropping every later wait from waitSites(); the real-file assertions would stay green because stale/broad only look at allow-listed finds and unlisted would be empty. Today's file has no such regex (grep over the file finds none), so this is latent.
findings.resolution: Cross-check the scan: assert that the count of primitive-call matches in the blanked text equals the count from a plain regexp over the unblanked text minus those inside comments, or fail when blank() ends with a different line count/bracket balance than the source. One assertion makes a desync red rather than silent.

findings.issue: The added paragraph says the `sed -n '/jobs:/,$p'` / `grep run:` read 'yields only `sh tools/verify.sh --only <slices>` calls' and that 'every CI job is setup plus one such call'. The read also yields non-verify.sh run steps: .github/workflows/ci.yml:115 (the `verified` job's ci-verified.py call, a gh/python step with no verify.sh) and the pip install / setup run steps at :226, :246, :271, :293. The sentence is a claim about the workflow that the workflow does not bear out literally.
findings.resolution: Reword to 'the gate itself is in `sh tools/verify.sh --only <slices>` calls; the other run steps are setup and the verified-run guard', keeping the pointer to `sh tools/verify.sh --list`.

findings.issue: _sweep_reading answers NOT_COLLECTED for any .py path that lacks a SWEEP_DIRS prefix. A bare basename (test_audit_task.py) is not a prefix match, so a real suite the sweep runs draws a false scope-gap. I confirmed by call: collects('test_audit_task.py','sweep','.') gives not-collected, and './plugins/audit/tests/test_a.py' gives not-collected too. tests_add_path accepts both spellings (_manifest_phases.py:922-931). The plan holds 44 bare-basename tests.add entries (P31.x, P26.x and others, all done or cancelled) under sweep-only gates (selftests, validate, lint). Before this diff the sweep was ignored, so runners was [] and those tasks started. Now runners is [sweep], the stop is block-only (DECISIONS scope-gap, drive-phase.py:467; widen refused at :2682 because config is None), and no vitest is needed to trigger it. This is F737-shaped: a false gap for a real Python suite under a gate that holds the sweep. The acceptance sentence 'no could-not-tell line' only covers the full-path spelling.
findings.resolution: In _sweep_reading, normalise a leading './' away. For a path with no directory component, or any path not under a root, answer COULD_NOT_TELL, or resolve it by looking for an existing file of that name under the roots. Reserve NOT_COLLECTED for a path that has a directory part, none of the roots prefix it, and no file of that suffix exists under a root. Add a case for the bare name and the './' form.

findings.issue: The 'no runner takes' stop treats the runner list as the gate's whole set of test commands, but entry_collector knows only vitest, jest, pytest and the sweep. A gate such as ['selftests', 'node --test x.test.mjs'], or sweep plus 'python3 -m unittest ...', has an unrecognised entry that runs the path. Before this diff the sweep was not counted, so runners stayed [] and the task started. Now the sweep makes runners non-empty, runners_taking returns [] for the .mjs path, and the task stops with 'no runner in this gate takes ...'. The only exit is block (config None, so widen is refused). Separately, the decision text offers 'widen|block' and does not say that the real cure is adding the runner entry to the gate or correcting tests.add. Pending P109.9 declares tests/audit/test__output.py under gate selftests and will now stop this way. That is probably a correct stop, but its message gives no remedy.
findings.resolution: Raise the 'no runner takes' decision only when every path-scoped gate entry resolved to a known collector. If any entry names no collector (entry_collector None and the entry is not a lint or validate), return the could-not-tell line instead. Make the message name the remedy (add a collecting entry to tests.gate, or correct the tests.add path). Add a case with sweep plus an unrecognised runner entry.

findings.issue: _sweep_roots takes every quoted string on a line and joins them with '/', so a compact or commented tuple becomes a wrong root silently. I called it: SWEEP_DIRS = (\n "tools", ".claude/hooks",\n) gives ['tools/.claude/hooks'], and a trailing comment like '# the "x" dir' gives ['tools/x']. A wrong root makes every real suite a false NOT_COLLECTED, and nothing reports it as could-not-tell. No case parses the real tools/sweep-selftests.py. Both new cases use fixture SWEEP_DIRS text (test__runner_collects.py:211-218, test_drive_phase.py:293-294). On today's file I checked it yields the five correct roots.
findings.resolution: Parse the tuple with ast.literal_eval or an AST walk, which handles os.path.join. If that cannot be done, treat any line holding more than one separate string argument, or a trailing comment, as unreadable and return None. Add a selftest case asserting that _sweep_roots on the repo's real tools/sweep-selftests.py equals its SWEEP_DIRS, so a reformat goes red rather than silent.

findings.issue: git ls-files -u in the task tree still lists stage 1/2/3 entries for both conflicted files (status UU), although the working-tree text has no conflict markers. A plain commit or commit-by-path refuses unmerged paths until they are re-added.
findings.resolution: Run git add on those two paths before the close commits (resolution is already correct in the working tree), and check git ls-files -u prints nothing.

findings.issue: _PLAIN_INTERPRETER_FLAGS is Python's flag set but _runs_first_path_as_program applies it to every name in _SCRIPT_RUNNER (bash, sh, ruby, perl, node...). Probed on the tree: `bash -s a/test_x.sh a/test_y.sh` is refused with 'runs a/test_x.sh as a program and hands it a/test_y.sh as arguments'. For bash, -s reads the script from stdin, so the first path is not the program and the sentence is false. This breaks the task's 'every refusal sentence must stay true'. It is contrived and only reachable through -s (-E on perl and -O on bash take an argument word, so they fall out as unread).
findings.resolution: Key the plain-flag table by interpreter, python-only for python*/py, and leave any option before the first path unread for the other runners. Or drop the letters whose meaning differs per interpreter (at least s, E, x, t) from the shared set.

findings.issue: The unbalanced-quote fallback in gate_entry_commands separates commands on bare operators only. It does not drop redirection targets, which the docstring says it does for the main path. `python3 a/test_x.py > a/test_y.py "x` (unbalanced) would count a/test_y.py as an argument and refuse with a sentence that is false of it. The entry is broken shell anyway, so this is low.
findings.resolution: In the fallback, skip the word after any token matching _is_redirection, or return no commands at all (read nothing) when the entry cannot be delimited.

findings.issue: The executor's trade-off makes the misroute stop effectively dead. `unclassified` collects every entry for which `_gate_derive.entry_collector` (_gate_derive.py:263-275) returns None, and that function only knows vitest/jest/pytest (UNIT_RUNNERS) and sweep-selftests.py. This repo's own meta.buildCommands (docs/audit/audit-plan.json) resolves validate, plugin-validate, gate, report, lint, shots and interactive to commands that all return None (read by running a json load of meta.buildCommands and matching each against entry_collector's rules); any gate the repo declares and that holds one of them (the phase gate certainly does) therefore makes `unclassified` non-empty, so `if not takers and unclassified` at :1166 always takes the could-not-tell branch and the `no runner in this gate takes %s` decision at :1175 is unreachable. It only fires for a gate made solely of vitest/jest/pytest/sweep entries, which real gates (lint, validate, build entries) almost never are. Acceptance (4) says the P130.38 misroute stops 'still fire', but only the test fixtures keep them alive (uc3 uses a single-entry gate, line test_drive_phase.py uc3, `(SWEEP_GATE,)`), not production gates. The could-not-tell line is also misleading for such gates: it names unclassified[0], which is a lint or validate entry, as the entry that 'may run' the suite.
findings.resolution: Count an entry as unclassified only when it can run tests: it names a suite path (`_phases.is_suite_path` on a `_phases.shell_word_path` word) or a known test module/runner token (`-m unittest`, `--test`, `mocha`, `tap`, `ava`, `node --test`, `npm test`). Lint, validate, report, shots entries are then ignored and the definite 'no runner takes this path' stop fires again for gates like this repo's. Name that qualifying entry (not unclassified[0] blindly) in the could-not-tell line.

findings.issue: No case holds the realistic shape: a known-runner gate plus a non-test entry (lint, validate). uc3 and uc4 use only the sweep or sweep plus `python3 -m unittest`, so the suite stays green while finding 1 holds; nothing pins that a lint-only extra entry leaves the stop in force.
findings.resolution: Add a case: gate (SWEEP_GATE, a lint command such as `ruff check .`) with a `.mjs` suite path expects the scope-gap decision, alongside the existing uc1/uc2 could-not-tell cases, which should keep a test-capable unclassified entry.

tasks.title: Every sweep leg is graded by the plain rules, and the codec leg's summary counts what it graded
tasks.description: Plan F1.1, invariant I15; absorbs P128.20 (register F677). (1) `grade()` in tools/sweep-selftests.py (def at :899 on 571becfd) loses its `encoding_pass` argument: a leg run under `--encoding`, alone or with `--spaced`, requires the `N/M cases passed` contract, counts cases, and reds a migrated file that prints the contract, exactly as the plain leg does. (2) A leg's heading names both conditions when both apply (`encoding pass (cp1252), spaced sweep`); each single condition keeps the heading it has today. (3) The codec leg's summary counts cases and migrated files the way the plain leg's does, so it never prints a count it did not take (P128.20's fault). (4) The grade-level case `g5` (:1721) goes; new cases run real children through `sweep()` in a scratch repository and assert: the codec reached the child; a live suite's cases are counted; a contract-free suite is red; a suite that swallows its own UnicodeEncodeError and exits 0 is red; a migrated file printing the contract is red; a combined-leg child sees cp1252 and a spaced, linked TMPDIR; the headings are pinned. tasks.title: The CI description says what main-run concurrency does, and the slice check and the CI verifier read every shape of the field they judge
tasks.description: Fault F730 (the P130.2 review, filed at docs/audit/evidence/returns/P130.2/20261017T230831Z.reviewer.json). Five defects in or beside P130.2's work. (1) .github/workflows/ci.yml:39-44 says a run on main 'is the record of what landed and is never cancelled'; `cancel-in-progress: false` protects only a RUNNING run, and GitHub still replaces a PENDING run when a newer one queues in the group `ci-refs/heads/main`. CHANGELOG.md:27 ('everywhere but `main`') carries the same implication. Fix: reword both to say a running main run is never cancelled and a queued one can be replaced - or key the concurrency group on the SHA on main so main runs never share a group, which makes the sentence true as written; the return names which was taken. (2) tools/gate-parity.py:1579: `slice_drift` classifies a job as release-tier only when its `if:` matches `_RELEASE_TIER_IF` and every other job as per-run, so a job with `if: ${{ false }}` or a push-only condition still counts as running its slices on every run, and `slice_drift` and `shard_matrix_drift` (:1609-1642) return []. Fix: a job `if:` counts as per-run only when it reduces to the verified-run guard the workflow puts on its jobs, optionally with the release-tier term; any other condition is a `problems` row naming the job and saying its condition cannot be proved to run on every run. A job that runs no `tools/verify.sh --only` call, such as the push-only `verified` guard job (ci.yml:97-99), carries no slice and stays outside this judgement. (3) tools/ci-verified.py:128-141: `decide()` matches a listed run on head_sha, path, status and jobs, never on its `event`, and `ask_github` (:153-170) does not keep it; a pull_request run's head_sha is the PR head while its checkout is the merge commit, so a PR run can vouch for a main SHA reached by fast-forward. Fix: accept only `workflow_dispatch` and `push` runs, append a `why` line naming the refused run's event, and fetch the jobs only of runs that can be accepted; the docstring's 'exactly this commit' then holds for every run it accepts. tasks.description: Fault F729. (2) tools/gate-parity.py:1579: `slice_drift` classifies a job as release-tier only when its `if:` matches `_RELEASE_TIER_IF` and every other job as per-run, so a job with `if: ${{ false }}` or a push-only condition still counts as running its slices on every run, and `slice_drift` and `shard_matrix_drift` (:1609-1642) return []. tasks.title: One function pair is the only way git path output becomes plan spelling and a plan path becomes a git pathspec, every site routes through it, and a lint names any listing call that does not
tasks.description: F740. Fourth recurrence of the two-path-bases class (F708/F709 in P130.14-ywo, F735 in P130.30-ywo), so an invariant replaces per-site patches. (1) THE PAIR. Two functions in plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py: `git_to_plan(path, git_root, project)` turns one path git printed (checkout-relative: status --porcelain, diff/show/log --name-only|--name-status, diff-tree) into plan spelling. `plan_to_git(entry, git_root, project)` turns a declared `files` entry into a checkout-relative pathspec, or None when it lies outside the checkout. Both handle both topologies: a member project (project directory under the git root, offset `member`) and `meta.gitRoot` below the project (offset `..`, plan spelling carries the `test/` prefix). The same directory is the identity. A git path outside the project is spelled with `../` so it cannot equal a declared entry. Callers that run git from the project with `ls-files`/`ls-tree` (cwd-relative output) or `--relative` must say so through a third argument or a named variant, not by skipping the pair. WHY THIS HOME: hooks may not import scripts/ and hooks/guard-bash-writes.py needs the pair, while scripts/ reach hooks/_config.py through `_loader.load_hooks_config()`, the one door `_deps` allows. `_loader` sits directly above `_output` in `_deps.LAYERS`, so every module that needs the pair can load it, including `_tree_stamp`, `_status_facts` and `_invariants`, which sit BELOW `_evidence_io` and could not import `_evidence_io.project_spelling`. Delete `_evidence_io.project_spelling` and `_status_facts._strip_git_root` and move their callers to the pair. Keep no second spelling. Also fix project_spelling's defect on the way: it returns the path unchanged when the git root lies below the project. (2) ROUTE every site of F740 through the pair. audit-lookup.py: `_phase_diff_paths` output, `DOCS_AUDIT_EXCLUDE` built from the project's docs/audit via plan_to_git rather than a literal, `_task_commit_diff_lines` and `_diff_lines` pathspecs (including the wave-tree arm), `existing_test_lines` output. integrate-task.py `undeclared_paths`. derive-phase-gate.py changedSince. run-test-gate.py: `_declared_by` / `classify_mutations` / `dirty_outside` / `_named_by_run` over `_tree_stamp.porcelain`, plus `task_changed_paths`' show-prefix arithmetic. _tree_stamp.py `dirty_digest` exclusion. _invariants.py commit-scope allow-list. audit-task.py `_declared_rels` / `_no_change_moves` (plan_to_git replaces `_invariants._rel(join(project, e), git_root)`). close-phase.py `uncommitted_declared` and the tip writer's prefix (`:1928`, `:2229`). hooks/guard-bash-writes.py dirty paths. tasks.description: F741. P130.18-ywo was recorded done at a commit holding only plan and evidence files: after a manual `start`, drive-phase `wave_step` (around :2644) ran it serially in the PHASE tree because a task was in_progress, while its work sat in the kept worktree (`close_wave` records it in keptTrees, read only when a new wave opens); the gate measured the phase tree (scopeDigest of the unchanged declared files), went green, and the close committed nothing of the task.
